summary: Built after the 1936 Greenstone Ridge Fire, rebuilt as a steel tower in 1964 on Isle Royale's Feldtmann Ridge; visitors may climb partway up.

facts.design: Pre-fabricated steel tower with a live-in steel cab

access.note: Inside Isle Royale National Park; the Park Service says visitors can climb partway up (page last updated February 2022).

visit.trail_note: Reached by the Feldtmann Ridge Trail, between Feldtmann Lake Campground and Siskiwit Campground; climbing is partway only.

events.note: Wikipedia ties the two wooden towers to the 1936 Greenstone Ridge Fire (built in response); the Park Service history page dates the first towers to 1939 (conflicts with 1936)
Park Service history page: CCC built the first fire towers at Isle Royale in 1939 (conflicts with 1936)
Old Feldtmann Fire Tower torn down, per Wikipedia
New tower assembled June 1964 by a Houghton, Michigan, contractor; Wikipedia infobox gives 1964 as built year
Wikipedia says abandoned by 1968; the nomination says use diminished after 1968 and eventually ended
Park Service: by 1980 none of the towers was occupied by fire lookouts; used as shelters until the mid-1980s
Added to NRHP January 5, 2021 as part of the Isle Royale National Park Fire Towers multiple property submission

corrections.why: The nomination measures the built tower at 41 ft 3 in from the concrete piers (about 12.6 m). The register's 40-foot figure matches the 1961 plan, which was never built as described.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1964 is when the tower was assembled and the build year in the infobox; Wikipedia's 1965 is the completion date. Both can be true.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on early dates and on the tower's history. (1) First towers: Wikipedia says 1936 and the NRHP nomination ties them to the 1936 fire without a year; the NPS Isle Royale page says CCC built them in 1939. (2) Old tower: Wikipedia says it stood near the new site and was torn down in 1963; the nomination puts it a half-mile away on Turkey Ridge. (3) Naming: the NPS Isle Royale page calls the re-established Turkey Ridge tower 'Feldtmann Tower'; the nomination uses New Feldtmann Fire Tower for the 1964 tower. Check which tower the Park Service means before any visit. (4) Height: the record's 12.2 m (40 ft, from NHLR) matches the 1961 plan; the built tower is 41 ft 3 in per the nomination and Wikipedia. Proposed correction to 12.6 m. (5) Abandonment: Wikipedia says by 1968; the nomination says use diminished after 1968 and eventually ended, with shelter use into the 1980s. (6) Access: climbing partway is from the NPS places page (updated Feb 2022); the NPS fire-tower page says the tower is no longer utilized. Current conditions and any closure are unverified. The NRHP nomination PDF is long; only targeted extracts were read, so the 1936 construction year for the old towers is not confirmed in the nomination itself. Reads: 5 distinct web pages plus one search; a local cache copy of an eastern lookouts list was checked and not used.
